original_title: PSA: Swap the radial ability menu in Star Wars Zero Company for more of a trad XCOM-style experience
summary_en: A recent discovery in Star Wars: Zero Company has players debating the game's control scheme. A simple setting change can transform the tactical experience from a radial menu to a more traditional linear interface, reminiscent of classic XCOM titles.

en.title: Star Wars: Zero Company Players Discover XCOM-Style Control Option
en.summary: A recent discovery in Star Wars: Zero Company has players debating the game's control scheme. A simple setting change can transform the tactical experience from a radial menu to a more traditional linear interface, reminiscent of classic XCOM titles.
en.body:
Many players diving into **Star Wars: Zero Company**, affectionately dubbed 'ZCOM' by some, have found themselves wishing for a more familiar control scheme. The game, which draws heavily from the **XCOM** series' tactical gameplay loop, features a radial ability menu by default. While designed with controller input in mind, this circular interface can feel cumbersome for mouse-and-keyboard users, requiring multiple pans to select actions and targets.

Thankfully, the developers have anticipated this desire for a more traditional experience. Buried within the game's options menu, under the Gameplay section and General area, lies the 'Ability Selection Style' setting. Players can switch this from the default 'Radial' to 'Linear'. This change shifts the action bar to a more conventional numbered row at the bottom of the screen, akin to the classic **XCOM** games, making it quicker and more intuitive to manage your squad's abilities during intense firefights. For those who can't quite commit, a 'Hybrid' option is also available, blending elements of both.

## A Familiar Interface for Tactical Fans

The shift to a linear ability selection is more than just a cosmetic tweak; it fundamentally alters the flow of combat for players accustomed to the **XCOM** formula. When lining up a crucial sniper shot or planning a complex flanking maneuver, having the ability icons readily available in a clear, horizontal list streamlines the decision-making process. This allows players to focus on the strategic positioning and tactical execution that makes games like **XCOM: Enemy Unknown** and **XCOM 2** so compelling, rather than wrestling with an interface that feels less suited to precise PC controls. The ability to quickly select 'Move', 'Shoot', 'Overwatch', or any character-specific skill without needing to re-center the camera or navigate a circular menu is a significant quality-of-life improvement for many.

## Community Embraces the Change

News of this hidden setting has spread quickly through the **Star Wars: Zero Company** community, with many players expressing relief and enthusiasm. Discussions on forums and social media highlight how this single option can elevate the game from a good Star Wars tactical experience to a potentially great one for a significant portion of the player base. The ability to tailor the interface to personal preference is a hallmark of well-designed PC games, and this discovery has reaffirmed faith in the developers' commitment to catering to their audience's diverse needs and expectations. It’s a small change with a big impact, allowing more players to truly immerse themselves in the strategic depth the game offers.

## What's Next

As players continue to explore **Star Wars: Zero Company**, further discoveries about its systems and potential for customization are likely. The developers have indicated ongoing support for the game, so players can anticipate future updates and patches that may further refine the gameplay experience based on community feedback.

content_raw: Star Wars Zero Company is enough like XCOM that everyone's been calling it ZCOM, but there are some ways it isn't quite XCOM enough for me. For starters, the radial menu you use to select each character's actions, a controller-friendly system that flings all your abilities out in a circle around the active character like a medieval jailer's ring of keys. The first time I panned over to find an enemy I wanted to attack and then had to pan back to the character I'd selected to pick an attack off their radial menu I found myself wishing for a more traditional way to play. And look at that, there it is in the options menu. Go to the Gameplay section, scroll down to Ability Selection Style at the bottom of the General area, and bump it from Radial over to Linear. (Image credit: Electronic Arts) That puts moving and shooting and overwatching and etcetera onto a numbered row of boxes down the bottom of the screen where God intended, getting them out of the way when you're trying to line up the perfect angle to punch someone into a wall from. There's also a Hybrid option if you're indecisive and feeling a bit "¿Por qué no los dos?" I'm still in the early hours of Star Wars Zero Company, but playing with a mouse and keyboard, Linear Ability Selection just feels better. Between this and the fact you can bother a gonk droid, maybe it is a 90% masterpiece like Ted says.
